external_only_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 on promoting the free movement of citizens by simplifying the requirements for presenting certain public documents in the European Union
external_only_references.review_state: Official English and Bulgarian EUR-Lex text for Articles 1–2 and 4 reviewed on 2026-10-25. Article 2(1) covers specified Member-State public documents presented to another Member State to establish listed facts including marriage, registered partnership, parenthood, adoption, domicile/residence and nationality; Article 2(3) excludes third-country public documents and copies of them; Article 2(4) excludes recognition of the document’s legal effects. Article 4 exempts documents within scope and certified copies from legalisation or similar formalities. This does not settle document recognition, all translation questions, or third-country document requirements. No local copy or topic-completion finding is implied.

external_only_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2019/1157 on strengthening the security of identity cards of Union citizens and residence documents issued to Union citizens and their family members exercising their right of free movement
external_only_references.review_state: Historical national citation only. EUR-Lex records the instrument as declared invalid in C-61/22 and replaced by Regulation (EU) 2025/1208 from 10 July 2025. See the Bulgaria source-dependency record for the national citation and transition issue. The Bulgarian route is recorded but not independently reviewed here. Do not treat this historical instrument as the current card-format rule.

external_only_references.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1208 on strengthening the security of identity cards of Union citizens and residence documents issued to Union citizens and their family members exercising their right of free movement
external_only_references.review_state: Official English text, instrument identity, application date, and Articles 7-8 were reviewed on 2026-10-25. The regulation applies from 10 July 2025; it sets the relevant residence-card format, title/code and transition provisions. The Bulgarian EUR-Lex route is recorded and its Article 7(2) code was compared in the source-dependency review. This reference does not establish Bulgarian implementation evidence or the status of an individual card. No local copy or topic-completion finding is implied.

external_only_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2023/2667 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the digitalisation of the visa procedure
external_only_references.review_state: Official English EUR-Lex instrument identity and amending scope verified on 2026-10-25. The regulation amends the Visa Code, VIS and other Schengen instruments. Detailed implementation dates and evidence of a functioning Bulgarian digital visa route were not reviewed. The Bulgarian EUR-Lex route is recorded but its text was not independently checked. No local copy or topic-completion finding is implied.

external_only_references.title: Council Decision (EU) 2024/210 on the full application of the provisions of the Schengen acquis in Bulgaria and Romania
external_only_references.review_state: Official EUR-Lex decision and Annex reviewed 2026-10-25. Article 1 and the Annex make the listed Schengen acquis applicable to Bulgaria from 31 March 2024; Annex item 5 expressly includes Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 (Visa Code), with an Article 3 exception to the extent not covered by Decision (EU) 2017/1908. This corrects the Bulgaria applicability statement in the 2023 Commission Notice for periods from 31 March 2024. Link-only reference; no local copy or national-topic completion is implied.

external_only_references.title: Council Decision (EU) 2024/3212 lifting checks at internal land borders with and between Bulgaria and Romania
external_only_references.review_state: Official EUR-Lex decision reviewed 2026-10-25. Article 1 lifts checks on persons at internal land borders with and between Bulgaria and Romania from 1 January 2025. This is later than the date on which the Visa Code became applicable under Decision (EU) 2024/210 and should not be used as that start date. Link-only reference; no local copy or national-topic completion is implied.
